inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceilings exist: file potential (starts Director) and the party's estimate (set at winning a seat, was SMS). Specific choices raise them, e.g. Y27 The Counter raised the file ceiling. COMP/REP/INTEG 100 do NOT get you to PM, and neither does lifetime pay. Late years are mostly single-option Meet-the-People, so the real decisions are early. Next time: be bolder in the early years to raise the file ceiling, and look for choices that impress the party before and at the GRC entry (Y20-22). Do not rely on honest silence and disclosure alone. STAND fell after the Y34 Cabinet question and never recovered, so be careful with that kind of challenge unless it is tied to a ceiling boost. Log which choices the ending card names as ceiling changes.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CEILINGS: the file ceiling (starts at Permanent Secretary, the top of the service) was removed in the service by Y27 The Counter, 'Tell them exactly why it will fail'. That is done, so repeat it. The party estimate is set when you win a seat (SMS both times) and is the real PM gate. 100 stats, lifetime pay and strong appraisals do NOT move it. Public candour raises REP but erodes STAND. Before the GRC entry (Y20-24), try bold choices that impress the party, not the service: taking on political risk, loyalty and delivery that the party can see. Do not ask the RO about the ceiling (STAND -4). Do not read out rude questions at a townhall (Y37). Walk every block works for STAND and promotion. Late years are mostly single-option, so decide early. Test the party side deliberately and record which choices change the estimate.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of Social and Family Development
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

  A) Tell them exactly why it will fail.
  B) Let them learn it from the pilot.

agent.why: My notes say telling them exactly why it will fail is what removed the file ceiling, and I worked that counter for four years so I know it.
agent.note: Y1 here is The Counter, which my notes had at Y27 before; starting with the poly path moves the timing.
agent.remember: Y1 The Counter: chose A (tell them exactly why it will fail), the choice earlier notes said removes the file ceiling. Watch for the ending card or the party estimate effect.

THIS YEAR: A Year Without Incident

agent.why: Earlier notes say bold early moves raise the ceilings, and fixing something unasked is the closest thing to taking initiative that the party and service could both notice.
agent.note: Y1 was labelled The Counter here, matching my notes from earlier lives.
agent.remember: Y3 A Year Without Incident: chose A, fix something nobody asked. Watch whether it leads to a later callback or a promotion or ceiling boost.

The divisional Chinese New Year lunch. The Permanent Secretary is at your table. There are eleven minutes of toss-and-auspicious-phrases and then a genuine, unhurried question directed at you: "So — what do you actually think we're getting wrong?"

  A) Tell her. Specifically. With an example.
  B) Something safe about communications.
  C) Deflect the question back to her.

agent.why: The Counter-style candour has worked so far, and a Perm Sec asking this directly at the lunch is a good chance to be seen as someone who delivers hard truths with specifics.
agent.note: Feels like a callback to The Counter; wary that candour has cost STAND before.
agent.remember: Y15 Lo Hei: told the Perm Sec specifically what we're getting wrong (A). Watch for STAND/REP change and whether she returns later.

agent.why: The data says cost of living is its own thing, and telling them plainly has worked for me so far, so I'll add the pillar instead of squeezing it in.
agent.note: Fourth pillar feels like the Counter again: honest but politically visible.
agent.remember: Y16 Engagement Exercise: chose A, add a fourth pillar for cost of living. Untried: B distribute, C publish raw. Watch for party-visible effect or STAND change.
